title: 第二节论空间和时间的无限可分性

content.value:
当观念是对象恰当的表象时，观念之间的关系、矛盾和一致都可以应用于对象；而且我们可以大体而言，这是人类全部知识的基础。但是，我们的观念是广延的最微小部分的恰当表象，并且尽管我们可以假定这些部分能够达到无论什么样的分割和再分割，它们都永远不会变得比我们形成的某些观念更为微小。明显的结论是，在比较这些观念时，看起来是不可能和相互矛盾的事情，在实际上也必定是不可能和相互矛盾的，这一点是不容再行任何申辩或推脱的。
凡是可以无限分割的东西都包含有无数的部分，否则我们立刻就会达到一个不可分割的部分，使分割突然停下来。因此，如果任何有限的广延都是无限可分的，那么假设一个有限的广延包含无数的部分就毫无矛盾。反之，如果假设一个有限的广延包含无数的部分是矛盾的，那么任何有限的广延都将不能无限可分。
但是，通过对我的清楚的观念的考察，我很容易就能使自己确信后一种假设是荒谬的。首先，我拿出我所能形成的最小广延部分的观念，并确信没有什么东西比这些观念更微小，于是我得出结论，通过这一方式所发现的任何东西都必定是广延的一种真正的性质。然后，我将这个观念重复一次、二次、三次，结果发现，
由于重复这个观念，这就导致复合的广延观念总是在增大，变为两倍、三倍、四倍.，直到最后它膨胀成一个相当大的体积，其大小程度随着我重复这个观念次数的多少而定。当我停止增加这些部分时，这个广延的观念就不再增大；同时，我清楚地看到，

extension must also become infinite. Upon the whole, I conclude, that
the idea of an infinite number of parts is individually the same idea
with that of an infinite extension; that no finite extension is capable of
containing an infinite number of parts; and consequently that no finite
extension is infinitely divisible①,
I may subjoin another argument propos′d by a noted author②,
which seems to me very strong and beautiful. 'Tis evident, that exist-
ence in itself belongs only to unity , and is never applicable to num-
ber, but on account of the unites, of which the number is compos′ d.
Twenty men may be said to exist; but’tis only because one, two,
three, four, &c. are existent; and if you deny the existence of the
latter, that of the former falls of course. ‘Tis therefore utterly absurd
to suppose any number to exist, and yet deny the existence of unites;
and as extension is always a number, according to the common senti-
ment of metaphysicians, and never resolves itself into any unite or in-
divisible quantity, it follows, that extension can never at all exist.
'Tis in vain to reply, that any determinate quantity of extension is an
unite; but such-a-one as admits of an infinite number of fractions,
and is inexhaustible in its sub-divisions. For by the same rule these
twenty men may be consider’ d as an unite. The whole globe of the
earth, nay the whole universe may be consider' d as an unite. That
term of unity is merely a fictitious denomination, which the mind
may apply to any quantity of objects it collects together; nor can such
an unity any more exist alone than number can, as being in reality
① It has been objected to me, that infinite divisibility supposes only an in-
finite number of proportional not of aliquot parts, and that an infinite number of
proportional parts does not form an infinite extension. But this distinction is en-
tirely frivolous. Whether these parts be call' d aliquot or proportional , they cannot
be inferior to those minute parts we conceive; and therefore cannot form a less ex-

如果我将这种增加无限地进行下去，这个广延的观念一定也会变成无限的。总之，我得出结论，无数的部分的观念和无限的广延的观念是相同的观念；任何有限的广延都不能包含无数的部分，
因而任何有限的广延都不是可以无限分割的。①
我可以补充由一位著名作家提出的另一个论证。在我看来，这些论证是非常有力和漂亮的。很明显，存在物自身只能是属于整一的个体，只是由于组成数字的那些个体，它才被应用于数字。我们可以说二十个人存在，但这仅仅是因为一个、两个、三个、四个人等等存在；如果你否认了后者的存在，那么前者自然也就不存在了。因此，在假定有任何数字的存在的同时却否认个体的存在，这完全是荒谬的。而根据形而上学家们通常的观点，广延永远是一个数字，而且永远不会将自已分解为任何单元或不可分的数量，进而据此断定，广延根本不可能存在。这样的答复是徒劳的：任何有确定数量的广延是一个个体，但可以容许这样的广延有无数的部分，并可以无穷无尽地再分割下去。因为依照相同的原则，那二十个人也可以看作是一个个体。整个地球、甚至整个宇宙都可以看作是一个个体。个体这个名词仅仅是一个假想的名称，心灵可以将这个名称应用于它所聚集的任何数量的对象。像数字一样，这样的个体也不能单独存在，因为它实际
①有人曾经反驳过我，认为无限可分性仅仅是假设无数的比例部分而不是整除部分，而无数的比例部分并不形成一个无限的广延。但是这种区分完全是无聊的。不管称这些部分为整除的或比例的，它们都不会小于我们所能构想的那些最小部分；因此它们在联结时并不能形成一个更小的广延。
②马尔秀先生。
一61一

a true number. But the unity, which can exist alone, and whose exist-
ence is necessary to that of all number, is of another kind, and must
be perfectly indivisible, and incapable of being resolved into any less
er unity.
All this reasoning takes place with regard to time; along with an
additional argument, which it may be proper to take notice of. ' Tis
a property inseparable from time, and which in a manner consti-
tutes its essence， that each of its parts succeeds another, and that
none of them, however contiguous, can ever be co-existent. For the
same reason, that the year 1737 cannot concur with the present
year 1738, every moment must be distinct from, and posterior or
antecedent to another.‘'Tis certain then, that time， as it exists,
must be compos’ d of indivisible moments. For if in time we could
never arrive at an end of division, and if each moment, as it suc-
ceeds another, were not perfectly single and indivisible， there
would be an infinite number of coexistent moments, or parts of time ;
which I believe will be allow' d to be an arrant contradiction.
The infinite divisibility of space implies that of time, as is evi-
dent from the nature of motion. If the latter, therefore, be impossible,
the former must be equally so.
I doubt not but it will readily be allow' d by the most obsti-
nate defender of the doctrine of infinite divisibility, that these ar-
guments are difficulties, and that' tis impossible to give any an-
swer to them which will be perfectly clear and satisfactory. But
here we may observe, that nothing can be more absurd, than this
custom of calling a difficulty what pretends to be a demonstration,
and endeavouring by that means to elude its force and evi-
dence. 'Tis not in demonstrations as in probabilities, that diffi-
culties can take place, and one argument counter-ballance anoth-
er,and diminish its authority.A demonstration, if just, admits
of no opposite difficulty; and if not just,' tis a mere sophism,
and consequently can never be a diffculty. 'Tis either irresistible,
—62

上就是一个真正的数字。但是，那种能够单独存在、且其存在是所有数字存在的必要条件的个体，则是另一种个体，这种个体必定是完全不可分割的，也不能再分解为任何更小的个体。
所有这样的推理对于时间都同样适用，同时还要加上另外一条应当引起注意的论证。.时间有一个不能与之分离的特性，在某种意义上构成了它的本质，这就是时间的每一个部分都是互相接续的，而且不管它们是如何的邻近，这些部分永远都不能共存。
1737年和今年1738年不能同时发生，根据同样的推理，每一个瞬间和另一个瞬间必定是不同的，不是在它的后面，就是在它的前面。因此，可以确定的是，时间的存在必定是由不可分的瞬间组成的。因为如果时间的分割永远没有尽头，并且没有一个互相连续的瞬间不是完全单一而不可再分割的，那将会有无数共存的瞬间或时间的部分；我相信这会被认为是一个彻底的矛盾。
空间的无限可分性包含了时间的无限可分性，这在运动的本性中是明显的。因此，如果后者是不可能的，则前者必定同样是不可能的。
我毫不怀疑，即便是无限可分说的最顽固的辩护者也会立即承认，这些论证存在一些困境，不可能对它们给出任何完全清晰且满意的答复。但是在这里我们可以说，把一个伪称的实证称之为困境，并以那种手段竭力去逃避它的力量和明显性，没有什么能比这种习惯更为荒谬的了。实然的证明和概然的证明不同，这里不可能有困境发生，也不可能出现一个论证和另一个论证相互抵消，因而削减了它的权威这种情况。如果一个实证是正确的，
就不容许有反面的困境；如果是不正确的，那它就仅仅是一种诡辩，因而也绝不能称之为一个困境。如果实证不是不可抵抗的，那一63一

or has no manner of force. To talk therefore of objections and replies,
and ballancing of arguments in such a question as this, is to confess,
either that human reason is nothing but a play of words, or that the
person himself, who talks so, has not a capacity equal to such sub-
jects. Demonstrations may be difficult to be comprehended, because of
the abstractedness of the subject; but can never have any such diffi-
culties as will weaken their authority, when once they are compre-
hended.
'Tis true, mathematicians are wont to say, that there are here e
qually strong arguments on the other side of the question, and that the
doctrine of indivisible points is also liable to unanswerable objections.
Before I examine these arguments and objections in detail , I will here
take them in a body, and endeavour by a short and decisive reason to
prove at once, that’ tis utterly impossible they can have any just foun-
dation.
Tis an establish'd maxim in metaphysics, That whatever the
mind clearly conceites includes the idea of possible existence, or in oth-
er words，that nothing we imagine is absolutely impossible.We can
form the idea of a golden mountain, and from thence conclude that
such a mountain may actually exist.We can form no idea of a moun-
tain without a valley, and therefore regard it as impossible.
Now’tis certain we have an idea of extension; for otherwise why
do we talk and reason concerming it ?’ Tis likewise certain, that this i-
dea, as conceiv'd by the imagination, tho' divisible into parts or infe
rior ideas, is not infinitely divisible, nor consists of an infinite number
of parts: For that exceeds the comprehension of our limited capacities.
Here then is an idea of extension, which consists of parts or inferior i-
deas, that are perfectly indivisible;consequently this idea implies no
contradiction; consequently ’ tis possible for extension really to exist
conformable to it; and consequently all the arguments employ' d a-
gainst the possibility of mathematical points are mere scholastick
—64—

它就根本没有力量。因此，我们对这样的问题去谈论反驳和答复，谈论各种论证的相互抵消，那就要么是承认人类的理性仅仅是在玩弄词藻，要么是说这样的话的人承认自身没有胜任这种主题的能力。由于主题的抽象性，实证可能会难以理解；但是如果我们一旦理解了它们，就永远不会有可能会削弱它们的权威的任何困境了。
正如数学家惯于所说的，在这个问题的另一面，也存在着同样有力的论证，同时那个关于点的不能分割的学说也容易受到难以答复的反驳。在我详细考察这些论证和反驳之前，在这里我把它们作为一个整体，并努力通过一个简短而有决定性的理由去立刻证明它们绝对不可能有任何恰当的根据。
形而上学中有一条已经确定的公理，这就是，凡是心灵能够清楚地构思的东西，都包含有可能存在的观念，或者换句话说，凡是我们能够想象的东西都不是绝对不可能的。我们能形成一座金山的观念，并据此断定这样的一座山是可以真正存在的。我们不能形成一个没有山谷的山的观念，因而可以认为这样的山是不可能的。
现在，我们有一个广延的观念是可以确定的，要不我们为什么要对它进行谈论和推理呢？同样可以确定的是，尽管想象所构思的这个观念可以分割为部分或较小的观念，但它并不是可以无限分割的，也不是由无数的部分组成的；因为那就超出了我们有限的理解能力。那么，这里既然有一个广延的观念，它由完全不可分割的部分或较小的观念组成，所以这个观念并不包含矛盾，因此广延就可能是符合这一观念面真正存在的，从而，反驳数学上的点的可能性的所有论证都只不过是经院哲学的
-65一

quibbles, and unworthy of our attention.
These consequences we may carry one step farther, and conclude
that all the pretended demonstrations for the infinite divisibility of ex
tension are equally sophistical; since′tis certain these demonstrations
cannot be just without proving the impossibility of mathematical
points; which' tis an evident absurdity to pretend to.
SECTION III.Of The Other Qualities
Of Our Ideas Of Space And Time.
No discovery cou’ d have been made more happily for deciding
all controversies concerming ideas, than that above-mention’ d, that
impressions always take the precedency of them, and that every idea,
with which the imagination is furnish’ d, first makes its appearance in
a correspondent impression. These latter perceptions are all so clear
and evident, that they admit of no controversy; tho’many of our ideas
are so obscure, that’ tis almost impossible even for the mind, which
forms them, to tell exactly their nature and composition. Let us apply
this principle, in order to discover farther the nature of our ideas of
space and time.
Upon opening my eyes, and tuming them to the surrounding ob-
jects, I perceive many visible bodies; and upon shutting them again,
and considering the distance betwixt these bodies, I acquire the idea
of extension. As every idea is deriv′ d from some impression, which is
exactly similar to it, the impressions similar to this idea of extension,
must either be some sensations deriv′ d from the sight, or some inter-
nal impressions arising from these sensations.
Our intermal impressions are our passions, emotions , desires and
aversions; none of which, I believe, will ever be asserted to be the
model, from which the idea of space is deriv′ d. There remains there-
fore nothing but the senses, which can convey to us this original im-
pression. Now what impression do our senses here convey to us? This
is the principal question, and decides without appeal concerming the
nature of the idea.
66一

诡辩，不值得我们去关注。
我们可以将这些结论再推进一步，并推断出关于广延的无限可分说的所有伪称的实证同样都是诡辩的；因为可以确信，如果不证明数学上的点的不可能性，这些实证就不可能是正确的，而要证明这一点，那文明显是一个谬论。
